page.layout: One column of text, with a heading at the top ("AD LECTOREM"), a verse poem of eight lines followed by a signature line, then a second heading ("EPIGRAMMA IOANNIS") with a subtitle line and a second verse poem. No margin notes. All on one printed page.

main_text.head: AD LECTOREM.

p.i: Quæ non accipiat porrecta fronte, probetúe,
Perge opera hac igitur studijs pd. sse scholarū,
Atq; etiam post hac Latia Graiaq; Camœnæ,
Quas habeant, per te fac retegantur opes.
Ringetur reliqui, qd tū? tibi fortibus aufis.
Nil obstet ceptum quin gradiaris iter.
Nec invidos timeas morsus: meliora tenetur.
Sit ua quis lacerat, jure docere tuis.

main_text.head: EPIGRAMMA IOANNIS Wonlichij Tig.
main_text.p:
Mollia crescētis nostra increpat otia vitæ,
Lumine nec placido Musa videre potest.
Cum te forte semel studijs operosa Minerua
Viderit, & gnauum divite mente beet.
Territa desidia ne in sœuam trasevat iram.
Munere nō privet, quod dedit illa, cave.
Nāq; et cura sagax, hæres et in artib. ardor.
Arte quod occlusum est, id reserare valet.
Tristia contemnens operi quæ tædia subsunt.
Et simul aspersus munere, diva, tuo.

page.notes: The first word of the epigram is a large decorated initial "M" joined to "ollia". Several lines of the first poem and the signature line are in italic type with long-s and ligature forms; a few words are doubtful and are marked [?]: "probetúe" and "tū? tibi", "qd", "tenetur" and "Sit ua quis" are read from a degraded scan. Line-ends in the second poem are not hyphenated. The first line of the first poem has a decorative initial "Q" with ligature "ua". The page image is slightly skewed and stained at the top; no page number, running head or signature is printed. Italic and roman type are mixed in the second poem; I have treated it as roman, as the scan suggests.
